fields.narrative_intro: *A rabid sloth and a dapper otter discuss the OpenRouter-Stripe acquisition at a VC pitch where the demo is actively hallucinating.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
DAPPER OTTER: "OpenRouter routes 10 trillion tokens a day."
RABID SLOTH: "Joined Stripe. Natural fit. Two great APIs."
fields.panel2:
[build]
DAPPER OTTER: "Stripe abstracts payments. OpenRouter abstracts AI brains."
RABID SLOTH: "The company that charges your card now picks your chatbot."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
RABID SLOTH: "They promised routing stays user-benefit-driven. Not Stripe's financial interest."
DAPPER OTTER: "The demo will confirm that."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: The pitch demo screen glows. It is routing every query to the most expensive model. A small coin-cha-ching animation loops silently. Both characters stare. A single dollar sign drifts past like a tumbleweed.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
DAPPER OTTER: "...it routed to GPT-4o. Twice."
RABID SLOTH: "User benefit."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: The demo screen now shows a Stripe checkout page. Line item: 'Definitely Not Financial Interest — $0.002/token.' The otter updates the pitch deck to read '10x growth, 10x fees.']

narrative_summary: The joke hinges on the deadpan irony of Stripe promising routing won't serve its financial interests — while the live demo silently routes every query to the priciest model and then literally opens a Stripe checkout.
rationale: Candidate 1 earns top marks across every axis: the deadpan voice is perfectly matched to the template, the specific detail of routing to GPT-4o twice lands as a real punchline rather than a restatement, and the final line item 'Definitely Not Financial Interest — $0.002/token' is the sharpest, most specific joke in the batch. The tumbleweed dollar sign in panel 4 is a genuinely fresh visual gag that the other candidates' monocle-drops can't match.
place: at a VC pitch where the demo is actively hallucinating
hat_pair: foam diploma scroll worn as a top hat with a tiny tassel dangling off
